updates.finding: The U.S. aviation secondary-sanctions pressure moved materially beyond the prior Baghdad/Muscat partial implementation. Reuters reported Iranian flights to Gulf neighbors including Dubai appeared cancelled on Thursday. The UAE General Civil Aviation Authority then officially announced suspension, effective Sep.24 until further notice, of flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the UAE, explicitly citing the U.S. ban. This is state-level implementation by a major regional aviation hub, but still does not establish worldwide grounding of all Iranian international aviation.
updates.status: IMPLEMENTATION BROADENED MATERIALLY; UAE OFFICIAL SUSPENSION CONFIRMED; GLOBAL SHUTDOWN NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.occurrence_time: 2026-09-24 (UAE local time; effective Thursday until further notice)
updates.drawer_effect: SUPERSEDE the Sep.23 status 'partial observed implementation limited to Baghdad/Muscat examples' with broader regional implementation. Preserve individual state/airport compliance and continuing-route evidence; do not convert Treasury's stated worldwide objective into an accomplished global shutdown.

updates.finding: The Saudi-led coalition said Saudi air defenses intercepted six ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis on Thursday, thwarting attacks directed at Taif and Yanbu. The coalition attribution and successful-intercept claim are official Saudi-led coalition claims at this horizon; independent weapon-by-weapon verification was not available in the sweep.
updates.status: SIX BALLISTIC-MISSILE INTERCEPTS CLAIMED BY SAUDI-LED COALITION; TARGET AREAS TAIF/YANBU; INDEPENDENT BDA LIMITED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Saudi-Houthi strike/intercept chronology and Yanbu threat drawer. Keep launch/target/intercept claims attributed to coalition unless independently corroborated; watch for debris, damage, casualty or Houthi target-claim updates.

updates.finding: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said they repelled multiple overnight Houthi attacks along the key Taiz-Aden supply route after hours of fighting. Reuters reported military-source confirmation from both sides that fighting occurred. The government success/disposition claim remains subject to later territorial and casualty corroboration.
updates.status: FIGHTING CORROBORATED; GOVERNMENT CLAIMS HOUTHI PUSH REPELLED; FINAL DISPOSITION/BDA PENDING
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE the existing Houthi Red Sea/South Taiz offensive drawer rather than create an isolated campaign narrative. Track whether the attack changed control of the logistics corridor and whether IRGC operational-support reporting can be tied to this specific action; do not infer that linkage without evidence.

updates.finding: The UN human rights chief said civilians are bearing the brunt of the expanding Yemen fighting. This strengthens the existing humanitarian-impact drawer as hostilities expand across multiple fronts. It should be reconciled with the Sep.22 UNHCR observed displacement figure above 130,000, at least 110 reported casualties including 28 deaths, and the separate projection that displacement could exceed 230,000; observed counts and forecasts must remain separate denominators.
updates.status: UN CIVILIAN-IMPACT WARNING UPDATED; EXISTING OBSERVED/PROJECTED DENOMINATORS REMAIN SEPARATE
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Yemen human-impact drawer with OHCHR warning; retain Sep.22 UNHCR actual displacement/casualty numbers and future displacement projection as distinct fields.

updates.update_type: maritime / commercial-data correction and trend update
updates.finding: Public reporting based on Kpler data said 10 commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday, a marked rise from the previously published Tuesday/early-week figures but still below the constrained recent average. This is a partial traffic recovery, not restoration of normal prewar passage. Commercial AIS visibility and methodology limitations remain material.
updates.status: PARTIAL TRANSIT RECOVERY; STILL DEPRESSED; COMMERCIAL-DATA CAVEATS APPLY
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Hormuz transit trend and preserve prior published counts rather than silently rewrite them. Flag the Wednesday 10-vessel figure for direct Kpler/Reuters-primary corroboration when proprietary or full updated commercial feed becomes available.

updates.finding: Reuters reported oil prices rose about 2% Thursday as U.S.-Iran diplomacy showed little sign of progress. This is market and diplomatic confirmation that the prior 'parties far apart/no agreement' status had not materially improved by this horizon; it is not evidence that talks ended.
updates.status: CONTACT CONTINUES; NO BREAKTHROUGH ESTABLISHED; MARKET PRICES PERSISTENT RISK
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE diplomatic-status drawer as no-breakthrough confirmation. Preserve contact-versus-agreement distinction and do not infer cessation of negotiations.

updates.finding: UK OFSI guidance published Sep.23 establishes an immediate presumption of denial for licence applications from Bank Sepah, Melli Bank plc, Bank Saderat, Persia International Bank and Bank Tejarat, except narrow legal/urgent circumstances. The existing general licence INT/2025/7628424 will not be renewed after Oct.22. The policy explicitly bars licences permitting UK-held funds to be remitted to Iran. This is a concrete tightening of financial access relevant to the existing frozen-assets/sanctions-pressure drawer.
updates.status: UK FINANCIAL-SANCTIONS LICENSING TIGHTENED; FIVE DESIGNATED BANKS IN SCOPE
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Iran sanctions/financial-access drawer. This strengthens restrictions on access/transactions but must not be described as confiscation or dissolution of Iranian assets. Track separately from U.S.-Iran bargaining over release of frozen assets.
